blocks.text: The date in verses 1–4 places this vision within Ezekiel’s narrated horizon, which begins with the 597 deportation, includes Jerusalem’s siege and destruction, and continues to restoration and nation oracles dated in the 570s BCE. Ezekiel 40 opens the final major section of the book (chapters 40–48), a vision that goes beyond this chapter’s measurements to include a sanctuary, returning glory, altar, priests and Levites, a prince, offerings, land, a river, tribes, resident aliens, and a city called YHWH-shammah. This practical outline can help readers follow the book’s movement, while not settling questions about its chronology or composition.
